title: Cyclic Hydrocarbons: Saturated Cyclohexane (C₆H₁₂) & Aromatic Benzene (C₆H₆)
tagline: Ring structures of carbon, covalent bond counts, and alternating multiple bonds.
theoryHtml:
Carbon atoms can link together not only in straight or branched open chains, but also in closed ring frameworks known as cyclic hydrocarbons:

1. Saturated Cyclic Hydrocarbon — Cyclohexane ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$):

In cyclohexane, six carbon atoms are joined in a closed ring by single covalent bonds, with two hydrogen atoms attached to each carbon atom:

  • Each carbon atom is bonded to two neighbouring carbon atoms and two hydrogen atoms, satisfying tetravalency.
  • Total Covalent Bonds: There are $6$ single $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bonds forming the ring and $12$ single $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bonds, making a grand total of $18$ single covalent bonds in a single molecule of cyclohexane.
  • Cyclohexane has the same general formula ($\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$) as straight-chain alkenes, but is completely saturated because it contains no double bonds.

2. Unsaturated Aromatic Hydrocarbon — Benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$):

Benzene is the parent member of aromatic hydrocarbons:

  • It consists of a closed hexagonal ring of six carbon atoms containing alternating single and double carbon-carbon bonds: $$\begin{matrix} \text{Three } \text{C}-\text{C} \text{ single bonds} \\ \text{Three } \text{C}=\text{C} \text{ double bonds} \\ \text{Six } \text{C}-\text{H} \text{ single bonds} \end{matrix}$$
  • Total Covalent Bonds: In benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$), there are $9$ carbon-carbon bonds ($3$ double $+ 3$ single) and $6$ carbon-hydrogen bonds, representing a total of $15$ covalent bonds.
pointsToRemember: Cyclohexane (C₆H₁₂) is a saturated cyclic ring containing 18 single covalent bonds.
Benzene (C₆H₆) is an unsaturated cyclic ring with alternating single and double bonds, containing 15 covalent bonds total.
Cycloalkanes share the general formula CnH₂n with alkenes, but possess no double bonds.
keyNotes: Exam Highlight: Count bonds carefully—Cyclohexane has 18 single bonds; Benzene has 3 C=C double bonds, 3 C—C single bonds, and 6 C—H single bonds (15 bonds total).

questions.question: Which of the following statements about diamond and graphite is INCORRECT?
options: In diamond, each carbon is covalently bonded to 4 other carbons in a 3D tetrahedral network
In graphite, each carbon is bonded to 3 other carbons in planar hexagonal sheets with delocalised electrons
Diamond conducts electricity while graphite is an insulator
Both diamond and graphite produce only carbon dioxide when completely burnt in oxygen
questions.answer: Diamond conducts electricity while graphite is an insulator
questions.explanation: Statement C is inverted. Graphite conducts electricity due to free mobile electrons, whereas diamond is an electrical insulator.

questions.question: What are the products formed during the complete combustion of ethanol in excess air?
questions.explanation: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O + heat and light.

questions.question: Why does mechanical agitation (beating on a stone, scrubbing with a brush, or rotating in a washing machine) aid the cleaning action of soap?
options: Mechanical force helps dislodge the oily dirt micelles from fabric fibers and disperse them into the wash water
Agitation turns hard water into soft water
Agitation heats water to boiling point
questions.answer: Mechanical force helps dislodge the oily dirt micelles from fabric fibers and disperse them into the wash water
questions.explanation: Soap micelles entrap grease, and mechanical agitation physically pulls and shears the dirt-loaded micelles off fabric surfaces into suspension.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid forms extensive intermolecular hydrogen-bonded dimers in liquid state, resulting in a higher boiling point (391 K / 118°C) than ethanol (351 K).

questions.question: What is the IUPAC name for CH₃—CH₂—CH₂—COOH?
questions.explanation: A 4-carbon continuous chain terminating in a carboxyl group (—COOH) is named Butanoic acid.

questions.question: What is the molecular formula and total number of single covalent bonds in a molecule of cyclohexane?
options: C6H12, with 18 single covalent bonds (6 C—C and 12 C—H bonds)
questions.answer: C6H12, with 18 single covalent bonds (6 C—C and 12 C—H bonds)
questions.explanation: Cyclohexane has formula C6H12; its ring contains 6 C—C single bonds and 12 C—H single bonds = 18 total bonds.

questions.question: How many double bonds and single bonds exist between carbon atoms in a molecule of benzene (C₆H₆)?
options: 3 carbon-carbon double bonds and 3 carbon-carbon single bonds (alternating)
questions.answer: 3 carbon-carbon double bonds and 3 carbon-carbon single bonds (alternating)
questions.explanation: Benzene features a planar ring with alternating three C=C double bonds and three C—C single bonds.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is an unsaturated cyclic hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Benzene is a closed cyclic hydrocarbon containing three carbon-carbon double bonds, making it unsaturated.

questions.question: What is the total count of covalent bonds (including all single and double bonds) in a molecule of benzene (C₆H₆)?
questions.explanation: Benzene has 6 C—H single bonds + 3 C—C single bonds + 3 C=C double bonds = 15 total covalent bonds.

questions.question: What is the molecular formula of cyclobutane (a saturated 4-carbon ring)?
questions.explanation: Like all monocyclic cycloalkanes, cyclobutane adheres to the general formula CnH₂n, giving C4H8.

title: Heteroatoms & Functional Groups: Halogens and Alcohols (—OH)
tagline: Replacing hydrogen with reactive heteroatoms and naming haloalkanes and alcohols.
theoryHtml:
Carbon forms bonds not only with hydrogen, but also with other elements such as halogens, oxygen, nitrogen, and sulphur. In hydrocarbon chains, when one or more hydrogen atoms are substituted by other elements such that carbon's tetravalency is preserved, the substituting element is termed a heteroatom.

What Is a Functional Group?

A heteroatom or group of atoms that confers characteristic chemical properties to an organic molecule, regardless of the carbon chain length, is defined as a functional group.

1. Halogens (Haloalkanes):

  • Heteroatom: Chlorine ($\text{Cl}$), Bromine ($\text{Br}$), or Iodine ($\text{I}$).
  • Formula of Group: $-\text{Cl}$ (chloro), $-\text{Br}$ (bromo).
  • Naming Rule: Named with the prefix 'chloro-' or 'bromo-'.
  • Examples:
    • Chloromethane: $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$
    • Chloroethane: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$)
    • Bromopropane: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{Br}$)

2. Alcohols:

  • Heteroatom: Oxygen ($\text{O}$).
  • Formula of Functional Group: $-\text{OH}$ (Hydroxyl group).
  • Naming Rule: Replace the terminal '-e' of the parent alkane with the suffix '-ol'.
  • Examples:
    • Methanol (Methyl alcohol): $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$
    • Ethanol (Ethyl alcohol): $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$)
    • Propanol: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{OH}$)
pointsToRemember: Heteroatoms are non-carbon, non-hydrogen atoms (e.g. Cl, Br, O, N) that replace hydrogen on carbon chains.
Functional groups confer distinct chemical properties to organic compounds regardless of chain length.
Haloalkanes use prefixes (chloro-, bromo-); Alcohols possess the —OH group and take the suffix '-ol'.
keyNotes: Nomenclature Check: Methanol is CH₃OH, Ethanol is C₂H₅OH; remember that the hydroxyl group in alcohols does not dissociate as OH⁻ ions (it is covalent, neutral).

questions.question: What is the functional group present in ketones?
questions.explanation: Ketones contain a non-terminal carbonyl group (>C=O) bonded to two other carbon atoms.

questions.question: In a homologous series, any two successive members differ by a formula unit of:
questions.explanation: Successive members of any homologous series differ by one carbon and two hydrogen atoms: a —CH₂— (methylene) unit.

questions.question: What is the difference in molecular mass between any two successive members of a homologous series (C = 12 u, H = 1 u)?
questions.explanation: Mass difference = mass of —CH₂— = 12 + (2 × 1) = 14 u.

questions.question: Saturated hydrocarbons burn in a plentiful supply of air with a:
questions.explanation: Complete combustion of saturated hydrocarbons yields carbon dioxide and water vapor, burning with a clean blue flame.

questions.question: Unsaturated hydrocarbons generally burn in air with a yellow flame with lots of black smoke because:
options: Their carbon percentage is higher and unburnt carbon particles form glowing soot
They react with nitrogen in air
questions.answer: Their carbon percentage is higher and unburnt carbon particles form glowing soot
questions.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons have a higher percentage of carbon that does not get fully oxidised in air, leaving unburnt carbon particles (soot).

questions.question: What is the definition of a 'heteroatom' in organic chemistry?
options: A carbon atom with an extra neutron.
Any non-carbon, non-hydrogen atom (such as oxygen, nitrogen, or chlorine) that replaces hydrogen in a hydrocarbon.
An atom that carries a radioactive charge.
questions.answer: Any non-carbon, non-hydrogen atom (such as oxygen, nitrogen, or chlorine) that replaces hydrogen in a hydrocarbon.
questions.explanation: Heteroatoms are non-carbon/non-hydrogen elements that bond to the carbon skeleton, forming functional groups.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula and IUPAC name of the two-carbon alcohol?
questions.explanation: The two-carbon alcohol is ethanol, having the molecular formula C₂H₅OH (or CH3CH₂OH).

questions.question: How does the suffix of an alkane change when converted into an alcohol containing the —OH functional group?
questions.explanation: In IUPAC nomenclature, alcohols are designated by replacing the trailing '-e' of alkane with the suffix '-ol' (e.g. Ethane -> Ethanol).

questions.question: Which of the following compounds contains chlorine as a heteroatom?
questions.explanation: In chloromethane (CH₃Cl), chlorine replaces one hydrogen of methane, acting as the halogen heteroatom.

questions.question: Why does an aqueous solution of pure ethanol (C₂H₅OH) fail to turn red litmus paper blue, despite possessing an —OH group?
options: The —OH group in ethanol is covalently bonded to carbon and does not dissociate into free hydroxide (OH⁻) ions in water.
questions.answer: The —OH group in ethanol is covalently bonded to carbon and does not dissociate into free hydroxide (OH⁻) ions in water.
questions.explanation: Alcohols are neutral covalent compounds; the C—OH bond does not ionise into OH⁻, so ethanol is neutral to litmus.

title: Functional Groups: Aldehydes (—CHO), Ketones (>C=O) & Carboxylic Acids (—COOH)
tagline: Carbonyl and carboxyl chemistry, structural formulas, and nomenclature rules.
theoryHtml:
Oxygen forms three other vital carbonyl-based functional groups in Class 10 organic chemistry:

1. Aldehydes (—CHO):

  • Structure: A carbonyl group ($\text{C}=\text{O}$) bonded to at least one hydrogen atom: $-\text{CH}=\text{O}$.
  • Position: Always located at the terminal end of the carbon chain.
  • Naming Rule: Replace '-e' of the alkane with the suffix '-al'.
  • Examples:
    • Methanal (Formaldehyde): $\text{HCHO}$ (1-carbon)
    • Ethanal (Acetaldehyde): $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ (2-carbon)
    • Propanal: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ (3-carbon)

2. Ketones (>C=O):

  • Structure: A carbonyl group ($>\text{C}=\text{O}$) bonded to two adjacent carbon atoms: $\text{R}-\text{CO}-\text{R}'$.
  • Position: Must be located inside the carbon chain (never terminal).
  • Minimum Carbons: A ketone must contain a minimum of 3 carbon atoms.
  • Naming Rule: Replace '-e' of the alkane with the suffix '-one' (pronounced 'own').
  • Simplest Member: Propanone (Acetone): $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$, widely used as commercial nail polish remover.

3. Carboxylic Acids (—COOH):

  • Structure: A carbonyl group joined to a hydroxyl group: $-\text{C}(=\text{O})\text{OH}$.
  • Position: Always terminal.
  • Naming Rule: Replace '-e' of alkane with '-oic acid'.
  • Examples:
    • Methanoic acid (Formic acid): $\text{HCOOH}$ (present in ant stings and nettle hair)
    • Ethanoic acid (Acetic acid): $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ (active ingredient in vinegar)
    • Propanoic acid: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$
pointsToRemember: Aldehydes have the —CHO group and take the suffix '-al' (e.g. Ethanal, CH₃CHO).
Ketones have the >C=O group inside the chain, take suffix '-one', and require at least 3 carbons (simplest is Propanone, CH₃COCH₃).
Carboxylic acids have the —COOH group and take the suffix '-oic acid' (e.g. Ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH).
keyNotes: Board Classic: Propanone (CH₃COCH₃) is the simplest possible ketone because the carbonyl carbon must be flanked by two carbon atoms on both sides.

questions.question: If the bottom of a cooking vessel becomes blackened on the outside while using a gas stove, it indicates that:
options: The air holes of the burner are blocked, causing incomplete combustion
The vessel is made of pure gold
questions.answer: The air holes of the burner are blocked, causing incomplete combustion
questions.explanation: Blocked burner air holes restrict oxygen supply, causing incomplete combustion and soot deposition on cookware.

questions.question: Which of the following reagents is a strong oxidising agent used to convert ethanol into ethanoic acid?
questions.explanation: Alkaline potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) and acidified potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇) add oxygen to oxidise alcohols to carboxylic acids.

questions.question: The addition of hydrogen to unsaturated vegetable oils in the presence of a nickel catalyst is known as:
questions.explanation: Hydrogenation is the catalytic addition of hydrogen across carbon-carbon double bonds to convert liquid vegetable oils into solid fats.

questions.question: Which catalyst is commonly employed during the industrial hydrogenation of vegetable oils?
questions.explanation: Finely divided Nickel (Ni) or Palladium (Pd) is used as a hydrogenation catalyst.

questions.question: Methane reacts with chlorine in the presence of sunlight to form chloromethane and HCl. This reaction is classified as a:
questions.explanation: CH₄ + Cl₂ xrightarrow{hν} CH₃Cl + HCl. Chlorine atoms substitute for hydrogen atoms one by one in a photochemical substitution reaction.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of carbon atoms required to construct a stable molecule belonging to the ketone family?
questions.explanation: In a ketone, the carbonyl carbon (>C=O) must be bonded to two other carbons, necessitating a minimum of 3 carbons (CH3COCH3).

questions.question: What is the IUPAC name and condensed formula of the simplest member of the carboxylic acid homologous series?
questions.explanation: Methanoic acid (HCOOH, commonly known as formic acid) has only one carbon and is the simplest carboxylic acid.

questions.question: Which suffix is attached to the parent alkane root to designate an aldehyde containing the —CHO functional group?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes take the IUPAC suffix '-al' (e.g. Ethanal, Propanal), distinguishing them from alcohols ('-ol').

questions.question: Which widely used cosmetic solvent (nail polish remover) is chemically known as propanone (acetone)?
questions.explanation: Propanone (acetone, CH3COCH3) is an organic solvent that rapidly dissolves nitrocellulose in nail varnish.

questions.question: What organic functional group is present in ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH)?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid features the carboxylic acid group (—COOH), composed of a carbonyl and a hydroxyl group.

title: Homologous Series: Structural Step (—CH₂—), Mass & Property Trends
tagline: Uniform chemical behaviors and regular gradations in physical properties.
theoryHtml:
A series of organic compounds in which the same functional group substitutes for hydrogen in a carbon chain, such that successive members differ by a constant structural unit, is called a homologous series.

Core Defining Characteristics of a Homologous Series:

  1. Constant Structural Difference:
    Any two consecutive (adjacent) members of a homologous series differ by exactly one $-\text{CH}_2-$ unit (methylene group).
    Examples: $$\text{CH}_4 \xrightarrow{+\text{CH}_2} \text{C}_2\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow{+\text{CH}_2} \text{C}_3\text{H}_8 \xrightarrow{+\text{CH}_2} \text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$$ $$\text{CH}_3\text{OH} \xrightarrow{+\text{CH}_2} \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \xrightarrow{+\text{CH}_2} \text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{OH}$$
  2. Constant Molecular Mass Difference:
    Since carbon has atomic mass $12\text{ u}$ and hydrogen has mass $1\text{ u}$, the mass of one $-\text{CH}_2-$ unit is $12 + 2(1) = 14\text{ u}$. Therefore, successive members differ by exactly $14\text{ u}$ in molecular mass.
  3. Identical Chemical Properties:
    Because all members possess the identical functional group, their chemical reactions are remarkably similar. For instance, all alcohols react with sodium to liberate hydrogen gas.
  4. Gradation in Physical Properties:
    As the carbon chain lengthens, the molecular mass and molecular surface area increase steadily. This strengthens intermolecular van der Waals attractions, resulting in a gradual increase in melting points, boiling points, and densities, alongside a progressive decrease in water solubility.
pointsToRemember: Successive members of any homologous series differ by a —CH₂— unit.
The difference in molecular mass between adjacent homologues is exactly 14 u.
Members share identical chemical properties but show a gradual increase in melting and boiling points as molecular mass rises.
keyNotes: Exam Highlight: Know the two key differences between successive homologues: a —CH₂— group in chemical formula, and 14 u in molecular mass.

questions.question: What gas is evolved when ethanol reacts with active sodium metal?
questions.explanation: 2Na + 2CH₃CH₂OH → 2CH₃CH₂O⁻Na⁺ (Sodium ethoxide) + H₂(g)↑.

questions.question: When ethanol is heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K (170°C), what product is formed?
questions.explanation: CH₃CH₂OH xrightarrow{Conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K} CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O. Hot concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent.

questions.question: What is 'absolute alcohol'?
questions.explanation: 100% pure, anhydrous ethanol without any water content is known as absolute alcohol.

questions.question: What is 'denatured alcohol'?
options: Ethanol rendered unfit for human drinking by adding poisonous methanol and blue dye
questions.answer: Ethanol rendered unfit for human drinking by adding poisonous methanol and blue dye
questions.explanation: Industrial ethanol is denatured with toxic additives (methanol, pyridine, blue copper dyes) to prevent unauthorized recreational consumption.

questions.question: What is 'vinegar' commonly used in pickles and food preservation?
options: 5% to 8% aqueous solution of acetic (ethanoic) acid
A mixture of ethanol and sugar
questions.answer: 5% to 8% aqueous solution of acetic (ethanoic) acid
questions.explanation: Vinegar is a 5–8% solution of ethanoic acid in water.

questions.question: What is the exact molecular mass difference between the second member (ethanol, C₂H₅OH) and third member (propanol, C₃H₇OH) of the alcohol homologous series?
questions.explanation: Consecutive homologues differ by one —CH₂— group, which corresponds to 12 + 2(1) = 14 atomic mass units.

questions.question: Why do the boiling points of alkanes increase smoothly from methane (-161 °C) to hexane (+69 °C)?
options: As molecular mass and chain length increase, the molecular surface area expands, strengthening intermolecular attraction forces.
Carbon atoms become lighter in larger molecules.
questions.answer: As molecular mass and chain length increase, the molecular surface area expands, strengthening intermolecular attraction forces.
questions.explanation: Greater molecular surface area strengthens intermolecular van der Waals forces, requiring more heat to boil.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of compounds belong to the SAME homologous series?
questions.explanation: Ethane (C2H6) and propane (C3H8) are consecutive members of the alkane homologous series (differing by —CH₂—).

questions.question: Why do all members of the carboxylic acid homologous series exhibit similar chemical properties?
options: They have the identical boiling point.
All members contain the same functional group (—COOH) which governs chemical reactivity.
They are all gases at standard temperature.
They contain identical numbers of hydrogen atoms.
questions.answer: All members contain the same functional group (—COOH) which governs chemical reactivity.
questions.explanation: Chemical reactivity is dictated by the functional group; since all carboxylic acids share —COOH, their reactions are similar.

questions.question: What is the fourth member of the alkene homologous series (starting with ethene as the first member)?
questions.explanation: 1st = Ethene (C2), 2nd = Propene (C3), 3rd = Butene (C4), 4th = Pentene (C5H10).

title: IUPAC Nomenclature of Carbon Compounds: Prefixes & Suffixes
tagline: Systematic naming of hydrocarbons, haloalkanes, alcohols, aldehydes, ketones, and acids.
theoryHtml:
To provide unambiguous identification, the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) established universal rules for naming carbon compounds:

Step-by-Step IUPAC Naming System:

  1. Identify the Longest Carbon Chain (Root Word):
    • $1\text{ Carbon} \implies \text{Meth-}$
    • $2\text{ Carbons} \implies \text{Eth-}$
    • $3\text{ Carbons} \implies \text{Prop-}$
    • $4\text{ Carbons} \implies \text{But-}$
    • $5\text{ Carbons} \implies \text{Pent-}$
    • $6\text{ Carbons} \implies \text{Hex-}$
  2. Identify the Degree of Saturation (Primary Suffix):
    • All single bonds $\implies \text{-ane}$
    • Contains double bond ($\text{C}=\text{C}$) $\implies \text{-ene}$
    • Contains triple bond ($\text{C}\equiv\text{C}$) $\implies \text{-yne}$
  3. Attach Functional Group (Prefix or Secondary Suffix):
    • Halogen: Added as prefix: 'chloro-', 'bromo-'. (e.g. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} \implies \text{Chloroethane}$).
    • Alcohol ($-OH$): Replace terminal '-e' with '-ol'. (e.g. $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{OH} \implies \text{Propanol}$).
    • Aldehyde ($-CHO$): Replace terminal '-e' with '-al'. (e.g. $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \implies \text{Ethanal}$).
    • Ketone ($>C=O$): Replace terminal '-e' with '-one'. (e.g. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 \implies \text{Propanone}$).
    • Carboxylic Acid ($-COOH$): Replace terminal '-e' with '-oic acid'. (e.g. $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \implies \text{Ethanoic acid}$).
pointsToRemember: Root words: Meth (1), Eth (2), Prop (3), But (4), Pent (5), Hex (6).
Suffixes: -ane (single), -ene (double), -yne (triple), -ol (alcohol), -al (aldehyde), -one (ketone), -oic acid (carboxylic acid).
Halogens are always written as prefixes (e.g., Chloropropane, Bromobutane).
keyNotes: Common Trap: Methanal is HCHO (an aldehyde); Methanol is CH₃OH (an alcohol). Do not confuse '-al' with '-ol'!

questions.question: Why is pure ethanoic acid known as 'glacial acetic acid'?
options: It is mined from glaciers in the Arctic
Its melting point is 290 K (17°C), so it freezes into ice-like crystals in cold weather
It reflects blue light like glaciers
questions.answer: Its melting point is 290 K (17°C), so it freezes into ice-like crystals in cold weather
questions.explanation: Pure ethanoic acid freezes at 17°C (290 K) into an ice-like crystalline solid, earning the name glacial acetic acid.

questions.question: The reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst to form a sweet-smelling ester is called:
questions.explanation: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH xrightarrow{H⁺} CH₃COOC₂H₅ (ethyl ethanoate ester) + H₂O.

questions.question: What is the primary commercial use of sweet-smelling esters?
options: Used in perfumes and as synthetic food flavoring agents
questions.answer: Used in perfumes and as synthetic food flavoring agents
questions.explanation: Esters have pleasant, fruity aromas and are widely utilized in perfumes, cosmetics, and food flavorings.

questions.question: The alkaline hydrolysis of an ester using sodium hydroxide to yield soap and alcohol is called:
questions.explanation: CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → C₂H₅OH + CH₃COONa (soap precursor). This alkaline cleavage of esters is termed saponification.

questions.question: Soaps are chemically defined as:
options: Sodium or potassium salts of long-chain carboxylic (fatty) acids
questions.answer: Sodium or potassium salts of long-chain carboxylic (fatty) acids
questions.explanation: Soaps are water-soluble sodium or potassium salts of long-chain fatty acids (such as sodium stearate, C₁₇H₃₅COONa).

questions.question: What is the systematic IUPAC name for the organic compound with formula CH₃—CH₂—CHO?
questions.explanation: The 3-carbon chain with a terminal aldehyde functional group (—CHO) is named propanal.

questions.question: What is the correct IUPAC name of the compound CH₃—CH₂—COOH?
questions.explanation: The compound contains 3 total carbon atoms with a —COOH group, which is propanoic acid.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct IUPAC name for CH₃—C≡CH?
questions.explanation: A 3-carbon hydrocarbon containing a carbon-carbon triple bond is named propyne.

questions.question: How is a halogen atom such as bromine incorporated into the systematic IUPAC name of an alkane?
options: As a prefix 'bromo-' before the alkane name (e.g. Bromoethane)
Halogens are never included in IUPAC names
questions.answer: As a prefix 'bromo-' before the alkane name (e.g. Bromoethane)
questions.explanation: Halogens are treated as substituents and prefixed with 'chloro-', 'bromo-', or 'iodo-'.

questions.question: What is the IUPAC name for the simplest ketone, CH₃—CO—CH₃?
questions.explanation: While commonly called acetone, its systematic IUPAC name is propanone (3 carbons with a ketone group).

title: Chemical Properties: Combustion, Sooty vs Clean Flames & Air Inlets
tagline: Complete vs incomplete oxidation, thermal energetics, and burner maintenance.
theoryHtml:
Carbon and its compounds are universally used as fuels because when burned in oxygen, they undergo combustion, releasing substantial amounts of heat and light energy.

1. Combustion Reactions:

  • Elemental Carbon: $$\text{C} + \text{O}_2 \longrightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{Heat & Light}$$
  • Methane (Natural Gas): $$\text{CH}_4 + 2\text{O}_2 \longrightarrow \text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Heat & Light}$$
  • Ethanol: $$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} + 3\text{O}_2 \longrightarrow 2\text{CO}_2 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Heat & Light}$$

2. Saturated vs Unsaturated Hydrocarbon Flames:

  • Saturated Hydrocarbons (Alkanes): Have a lower carbon percentage and burn with a clean, blue, non-sooty flame in an adequate supply of air, resulting in complete combustion.
  • Unsaturated Hydrocarbons (Alkenes & Alkynes): Possess a significantly higher carbon-to-hydrogen ratio. They do not get fully oxidised in ordinary atmospheric air, burning with a yellow, luminous, and sooty flame that deposits unburned carbon soot on surfaces.
🔬 Daily Life Problem: Blackening of Cooking Pots

At home, gas stoves have small air inlets at their base. When these air inlets get clogged with dirt or grease, the supply of oxygen is restricted. Saturated fuel gas (LPG) undergoes incomplete combustion, producing a smoky yellow flame that deposits unburnt black soot on the bottoms of cooking vessels. Cleaning the air holes restores the clean blue flame!
pointsToRemember: Complete combustion of carbon compounds produces CO₂, H₂O, heat, and light.
Saturated hydrocarbons burn with a clean blue flame in sufficient oxygen.
Unsaturated hydrocarbons or incomplete combustion in limited air produces a yellow sooty flame that blackens cooking vessels.
keyNotes: Practical Reasoning Question: Why do cooking pots get blackened at the bottom? Because air inlets of the burner are blocked, causing incomplete combustion and soot formation.

questions.question: What gas is released with brisk effervescence when ethanoic acid reacts with sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO₃)?
questions.explanation: CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂(g)↑. The carbon dioxide gas produces vigorous effervescence and turns lime water milky.

questions.question: What are the two structural features of a soap molecule in aqueous solution?
options: A hydrophilic ionic head (water-soluble) and a hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail (oil-soluble)
An acidic head and basic tail
questions.answer: A hydrophilic ionic head (water-soluble) and a hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail (oil-soluble)
questions.explanation: A soap molecule has an ionic head (—COO⁻Na⁺) which is hydrophilic (water-attracting) and a long non-polar hydrocarbon chain tail which is hydrophobic (oil-attracting).

questions.question: In a soap micelle formed in water, how are the soap molecules oriented around an oily dirt droplet?
options: Hydrophobic tails point inwards towards the oil droplet, and hydrophilic ionic heads face outward towards water
Hydrophilic heads point inwards and hydrophobic tails point outwards
questions.answer: Hydrophobic tails point inwards towards the oil droplet, and hydrophilic ionic heads face outward towards water
questions.explanation: The hydrophobic alkyl tails dissolve in the central oily dirt, while the charged ionic heads project outwards into water, forming a stable emulsion.

questions.question: Why does a soap solution appear cloudy or translucent?
options: Soap micelles are large colloidal clusters that scatter light (Tyndall effect)
questions.answer: Soap micelles are large colloidal clusters that scatter light (Tyndall effect)
questions.explanation: Colloidal soap micelles aggregate into clusters of sufficient particle size to scatter visible light rays, giving the solution a cloudy appearance.

questions.question: What causes the formation of an insoluble curdy precipitate (scum) when soap is used in hard water?
options: Reaction of soap with dissolved sodium chloride
Reaction of soap with Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions present in hard water to form insoluble calcium and magnesium salts
questions.answer: Reaction of soap with Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions present in hard water to form insoluble calcium and magnesium salts
questions.explanation: 2RCOO⁻Na⁺ + Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ → (RCOO)₂Ca/Mg↓ (insoluble scum) + 2Na⁺, precipitating the soap and reducing its lathering power.

questions.question: What are the chemical products formed during the complete combustion of methane (CH₄) in excess oxygen?
options: Carbon dioxide, water vapour, heat, and light
questions.answer: Carbon dioxide, water vapour, heat, and light
questions.explanation: Complete combustion yields carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water (H₂O), alongside substantial heat and light.

questions.question: Why does an unsaturated hydrocarbon like ethyne burn with a yellow, smoky flame when ignited in ordinary atmospheric air?
options: Its high carbon percentage cannot be completely oxidised by the limited oxygen in air, leaving unburnt incandescent carbon particles (soot).
Ethyne does not react with oxygen.
questions.answer: Its high carbon percentage cannot be completely oxidised by the limited oxygen in air, leaving unburnt incandescent carbon particles (soot).
questions.explanation: High carbon content leads to incomplete combustion in air; unburned glowing carbon particles produce a smoky yellow flame.

questions.question: While cooking, if the bottom of the cooking vessel is getting blackened on the outside, it clearly signifies that:
options: The fuel is not burning completely due to insufficient air supply through blocked burner vents.
The vessel is made of pure diamond.
questions.answer: The fuel is not burning completely due to insufficient air supply through blocked burner vents.
questions.explanation: Blackening indicates soot deposition from incomplete combustion caused by blocked air holes at the burner base.

questions.question: Why are coal and petroleum termed fossil fuels that release smoke and acidic pollutants when burned?
options: They are synthetic plastics made in chemical factories.
They were formed from ancient biological biomass and contain small amounts of nitrogen and sulphur that burn into acidic oxides (NOx, SOx).
questions.answer: They were formed from ancient biological biomass and contain small amounts of nitrogen and sulphur that burn into acidic oxides (NOx, SOx).
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels contain nitrogen and sulphur impurities that oxidise during combustion to form harmful acidic oxides causing acid rain.

questions.question: Write the balanced chemical equation for the complete combustion of ethanol (C₂H₅OH):
questions.explanation: Complete combustion of one mole of ethanol requires 3 moles of oxygen to yield 2 moles of CO₂ and 3 moles of H₂O.

title: Chemical Properties: Oxidation of Alcohols & Hydrogenation of Oils
tagline: Alkaline KMnO₄, acidified K₂Cr₂O₇, and the industrial synthesis of vegetable ghee.
theoryHtml:
1. Controlled Oxidation of Alcohols:

While combustion is rapid, uncontrolled oxidation that completely degrades carbon chains into $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, carbon compounds can also undergo controlled chemical oxidation.

Alcohols can be converted into carboxylic acids using powerful oxidising agents (substances that supply nascent oxygen):

  • Reagents: Alkaline Potassium Permanganate ($\text{alkaline }\text{KMnO}_4 + \Delta$) OR Acidified Potassium Dichromate ($\text{acidified }\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + \Delta$).
  • Reaction: $$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{Alkaline }\text{KMnO}_4 + \Delta \quad\text{or}\quad \text{Acidified }\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + \Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$ Ethanol is cleanly oxidised to ethanoic acid.

2. Addition Reaction (Hydrogenation of Vegetable Oils):

Unsaturated hydrocarbons add hydrogen across their carbon-carbon multiple bonds in the presence of finely divided metal catalysts (such as Nickel, $\text{Ni}$ or Palladium, $\text{Pd}$) to yield saturated hydrocarbons:

$R_2\text{C}=\text{C}R_2 + \text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni catalyst, } 200\ ^\circ\text{C}} R_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}R_2$

Industrial & Nutritional Significance:

  • Hydrogenation of Oils: Liquid vegetable oils (like groundnut, mustard, sunflower oil) contain long unsaturated fatty acid chains with double bonds. Treating them with hydrogen over a nickel catalyst converts them into solid, saturated fats known commercially as vanaspati ghee.
  • Health Advisory: Vegetable oils containing unsaturated fatty acids are healthy for cardiovascular consumption. In contrast, saturated animal fats and hydrogenated fats contain saturated fatty acids that elevate blood cholesterol and are harmful to heart health.
pointsToRemember: Ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid using alkaline KMnO₄ or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ as oxidising agents.
Unsaturated hydrocarbons undergo addition reactions with H₂ in the presence of a Nickel (Ni) catalyst.
Industrial hydrogenation converts liquid unsaturated vegetable oils into solid saturated fats (vanaspati ghee).
keyNotes: Core Board Questions: Name the oxidising agents for ethanol to ethanoic acid (alkaline KMnO₄ / acidified K₂Cr₂O₇) and state the industrial use of addition reactions (hydrogenation of vegetable oils using Ni catalyst).

questions.question: Synthetic detergents are superior to soaps for washing in hard water because:
options: Their charged sulphonate/ammonium ends do not form insoluble precipitates with Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions
questions.answer: Their charged sulphonate/ammonium ends do not form insoluble precipitates with Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions
questions.explanation: Detergents are sodium salts of sulphonic acids or ammonium salts whose calcium and magnesium salts are water-soluble, preventing scum formation.

questions.question: What is the chemical name and molecular formula of the simplest alkyne?
questions.explanation: Ethyne (common name acetylene, H—C≡C—H) is the simplest alkyne with formula C₂H₂.

questions.question: What is the formula of the organic compound cyclopentane?
questions.explanation: Cyclopentane is a ring of 5 —CH₂— groups with formula C₅H₁₀.

questions.question: How can you experimentally distinguish between an alcohol (ethanol) and a carboxylic acid (ethanoic acid)?
options: Ethanol turns blue litmus red, whereas ethanoic acid does not
Ethanoic acid reacts with NaHCO₃ with brisk effervescence of CO₂ gas, whereas ethanol does not react with NaHCO₃
Ethanol dissolves in water but ethanoic acid is insoluble
questions.answer: Ethanoic acid reacts with NaHCO₃ with brisk effervescence of CO₂ gas, whereas ethanol does not react with NaHCO₃
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃) to evolve CO₂ gas with brisk effervescence (lime water test), while alcohols do not react.

questions.question: Why is a mixture of ethyne (acetylene) and pure oxygen burnt for welding metals, whereas a mixture of ethyne and air is NOT used?
options: Air contains only ~21% O₂, causing incomplete combustion with a smoky flame; pure O₂ ensures complete combustion reaching 3000°C
Ethyne reacts with nitrogen in air to form poisonous cyanide gas
Ethyne does not ignite in air
questions.answer: Air contains only ~21% O₂, causing incomplete combustion with a smoky flame; pure O₂ ensures complete combustion reaching 3000°C
questions.explanation: Burning ethyne in air results in incomplete combustion due to insufficient oxygen, generating a low-temperature sooty flame. Pure oxygen produces an intensely hot (~3000°C) oxy-acetylene flame suitable for cutting and welding.

questions.question: Which of the following chemical reagents is used as a strong oxidising agent to convert ethanol directly into ethanoic acid?
questions.explanation: Alkaline KMnO₄ or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ supplies oxygen to oxidise the alcohol group (—CH₂OH) into a carboxylic acid (—COOH).

questions.question: What metal catalyst is universally employed in the industrial hydrogenation of vegetable oils into solid cooking fats?
questions.explanation: Finely divided nickel (Ni) or palladium acts as a heterogeneous catalyst to add hydrogen across C=C double bonds.

questions.question: From a human health and nutritional standpoint, why are natural vegetable oils preferred over saturated animal fats or hydrogenated vanaspati ghee?
options: Vegetable oils contain unsaturated fatty acids which are healthy, whereas saturated fats increase blood cholesterol and cardiovascular risk.
Hydrogenated fats turn into sugar in the stomach.
questions.answer: Vegetable oils contain unsaturated fatty acids which are healthy, whereas saturated fats increase blood cholesterol and cardiovascular risk.
questions.explanation: Unsaturated fatty acids promote cardiovascular health; saturated and trans fats lead to arterial plaque and heart disease.

questions.question: Which of the following hydrocarbons will undergo an addition reaction with hydrogen in the presence of a nickel catalyst?
questions.explanation: Only unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes like C3H6 or alkynes) possess multiple bonds capable of undergoing addition reactions.

questions.question: What chemical change takes place when purple alkaline KMnO₄ is warmed with ethanol?
options: Ethanol turns into pure carbon soot.
The purple color of KMnO₄ discharges as it oxidises ethanol into ethanoic acid.
questions.answer: The purple color of KMnO₄ discharges as it oxidises ethanol into ethanoic acid.
questions.explanation: As permanganate ions transfer oxygen to ethanol, MnO4⁻ is reduced to brown MnO₂, discharging the deep purple coloration.

title: Chemical Properties: Substitution Reactions of Alkanes (Chlorination)
tagline: Stepwise photochemical chlorination of methane in the presence of sunlight.
theoryHtml:
Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) are generally unreactive and inert towards acids, bases, and common laboratory reagents because all valence bonds are fully satisfied single covalent bonds.

However, in the presence of sunlight (ultraviolet light, $h\nu$), alkanes undergo rapid reactions with halogens. Chlorine can replace the hydrogen atoms of an alkane one by one in a process called a substitution reaction.

Stepwise Photochemical Chlorination of Methane:

When methane and chlorine are mixed in diffused sunlight, chlorine atoms successively displace hydrogen atoms:

  1. Formation of Chloromethane (Methyl Chloride): $$\text{CH}_4 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Sunlight}} \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{HCl}$$
  2. Formation of Dichloromethane (Methylene Chloride): $$\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Sunlight}} \text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2 + \text{HCl}$$
  3. Formation of Trichloromethane (Chloroform): $$\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Sunlight}} \text{CHCl}_3 + \text{HCl}$$
  4. Formation of Tetrachloromethane (Carbon Tetrachloride): $$\text{CHCl}_3 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Sunlight}} \text{CCl}_4 + \text{HCl}$$

Why Is It Called a Substitution Reaction?

Because an atom of one element (chlorine) substitutes (takes the place of) an atom of another element (hydrogen) on the carbon chain without altering the saturated single-bond backbone.
pointsToRemember: Saturated alkanes undergo substitution reactions with chlorine in the presence of sunlight.
Chlorine replaces hydrogen atoms one by one, forming CH₃Cl, CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃ (chloroform), and CCl₄.
A substitution reaction is one where an atom or group replaces another atom or group on a molecule.
keyNotes: Exam Point: Sunlight is essential for the chlorination of methane because UV photons provide the energy to dissociate Cl₂ into reactive free radical chlorine atoms.

questions.question: Which of the following hydrocarbons will undergo catalytic addition reaction with hydrogen in the presence of nickel: C₂H₆, C₃H₈, C₃H₆, C₂H₂, CH₄?
questions.explanation: Only unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes like C₃H₆ and alkynes like C₂H₂) possess double/triple bonds capable of undergoing catalytic addition of hydrogen.

questions.question: Why will soap NOT form micelles when dissolved in ethanol?
options: The hydrophobic alkyl tail of soap is soluble in organic ethanol, so it does not need to cluster inward to escape the solvent
questions.answer: The hydrophobic alkyl tail of soap is soluble in organic ethanol, so it does not need to cluster inward to escape the solvent
questions.explanation: Micelle formation is driven by the hydrophobic effect in polar water. In non-polar/organic solvents like ethanol, the hydrocarbon tail dissolves freely throughout the solvent, precluding micelle aggregation.

questions.question: Why does the intake of even a tiny quantity of methanol cause permanent blindness and death?
options: Methanol is oxidised to methanal in the liver, which coagulates cellular protoplasm and destroys the optic nerve
Methanol absorbs all oxygen from hemoglobin
questions.answer: Methanol is oxidised to methanal in the liver, which coagulates cellular protoplasm and destroys the optic nerve
questions.explanation: Alcohol dehydrogenase in the liver oxidises methanol (CH₃OH) to methanal (HCHO, formaldehyde). Methanal rapidly cross-links and coagulates cell proteins (like egg albumin during cooking) and attacks retinal cells/optic nerve.

questions.question: What is the chemical reaction when ethanoic acid is reacted with sodium hydroxide solution?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid reacts with sodium hydroxide in a typical acid-base neutralisation to form sodium ethanoate (sodium acetate) and water.

questions.question: What is the structural formula of ethyne?
questions.explanation: Ethyne has two carbon atoms connected by a triple covalent bond: H—C≡C—H.

questions.question: What essential reaction condition is required for the chlorination of methane to proceed at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Sunlight provides ultraviolet photons that break the Cl—Cl bond homolytically to initiate the free radical substitution.

questions.question: What is the common trivial name of trichloromethane (CHCl₃), an organic liquid historically used as a general anaesthetic?
questions.explanation: Trichloromethane (CHCl₃) is universally known as chloroform, an effective solvent and historical anaesthetic.

questions.question: Why is the reaction between methane and chlorine classified specifically as a 'substitution reaction'?
options: A chlorine atom replaces (substitutes for) a hydrogen atom bonded to carbon.
Chlorine adds to a double bond.
questions.answer: A chlorine atom replaces (substitutes for) a hydrogen atom bonded to carbon.
questions.explanation: Substitution occurs when one atom (Cl) displaces another atom (H) from a carbon framework without breaking the chain.

questions.question: What final fully chlorinated product is obtained when methane reacts with excess chlorine in bright sunlight?
questions.explanation: In excess chlorine, all four hydrogen atoms are successively replaced, yielding carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄).

questions.question: In the reaction CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl, what inorganic acidic gas is evolved as a byproduct?
questions.explanation: The displaced hydrogen combines with a chlorine atom to form hydrogen chloride gas (HCl).

title: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH): Reactions with Sodium, Dehydration & Toxicity
tagline: Sodium ethoxide effervescence, catalytic dehydration to ethene, and physiological effects.
theoryHtml:
Ethanol ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$, commonly called ethyl alcohol or simply alcohol) is the second member of the alcohol series. It is a clear, colorless liquid at room temperature with a characteristic pleasant odor and a boiling point of $78\ ^\circ\text{C}$ ($351\text{ K}$). It is miscible with water in all proportions.

1. Key Chemical Reactions of Ethanol:

  • Reaction with Sodium Metal:
    Ethanol reacts gently with active sodium metal to produce effervescence of hydrogen gas and a soluble salt called sodium ethoxide: $$2\text{Na} + 2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \longrightarrow 2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{ONa} + \text{H}_2(g) \uparrow$$ This reaction is used as a laboratory test to detect alcohols.
  • Dehydration of Ethanol to Ethene:
    Heating ethanol with excess concentrated sulphuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) at $443\text{ K}$ ($170\ ^\circ\text{C}$) removes a molecule of water to produce the unsaturated alkene ethene: $$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{Hot conc. }\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4,\; 443\text{ K}} \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$ In this reaction, concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a powerful dehydrating agent (removes water from molecules).

2. Biological & Physiological Effects of Alcohols:

  • Ethanol Toxicity: Ingestion of ethanol depresses the central nervous system, impairs muscle coordination, slows reflexes, dulls cognitive judgment, and causes long-term liver cirrhosis.
  • Methanol Poisoning: Ingestion of even minute quantities of methanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$) is lethal. Methanol is oxidised in the liver by enzymes to methanal ($\text{HCHO}$), which rapidly coagulates cell protoplasm (just as an egg coagulates when boiled) and attacks the optic nerve, causing permanent blindness and respiratory failure.
  • Denatured Alcohol: To prevent the misuse of cheap industrial alcohol for drinking, it is 'denatured' by adding poisonous methanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$), foul-smelling pyridine, and a blue dye (copper sulphate) so it can be easily identified.
pointsToRemember: Ethanol reacts with sodium to form sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas: 2Na + 2C₂H₅OH → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂.
Heating ethanol with excess conc. H₂SO₄ at 443 K dehydrates it to ethene (C₂H₄); conc. H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent.
Denatured alcohol contains toxic methanol and blue dye to prevent recreational consumption.
keyNotes: Crucial Temperature: Dehydration of ethanol requires exactly 443 K (170 °C) with excess conc. H₂SO₄ to produce ethene!

questions.question: An organic compound 'A' (molecular formula C₂H₆O) on oxidation with alkaline KMnO₄ gives compound 'B' (C₂H₄O₂). When 'A' and 'B' are warmed together in the presence of conc. H₂SO₄, a sweet-smelling compound 'C' is formed. Compound 'C' on treatment with aqueous NaOH regenerates 'A' and produces sodium ethanoate. Identify A, B, and C:
options: A = Ethanol, B = Ethanoic acid, C = Ethyl ethanoate
A = Methanol, B = Methanoic acid, C = Methyl methanoate
A = Ethanoic acid, B = Ethanol, C = Acetone
A = Propanol, B = Propanoic acid, C = Propyl propanoate
questions.answer: A = Ethanol, B = Ethanoic acid, C = Ethyl ethanoate
questions.explanation: Ethanol (A, C₂H₆O) oxidises to Ethanoic acid (B, C₂H₄O₂). Esterification gives Ethyl ethanoate (C, CH₃COOC₂H₅). Saponification of C with NaOH yields ethanol (A) + sodium ethanoate.

questions.question: What is the total number of electron pairs shared (total covalent bonds) in a molecule of ethyne (C₂H₂)?
questions.explanation: In H—C≡C—H, there are two C—H single bonds (2 pairs) and one C≡C triple bond (3 pairs), totaling 5 shared pairs of electrons (10 shared electrons).

questions.question: An unsaturated hydrocarbon 'X' on complete hydrogenation with 2 moles of H₂ gas in the presence of a nickel catalyst yields n-butane (C₄H₁₀). How many triple bonds or double bonds were present in compound 'X'?
options: One triple bond (or two double bonds)
questions.answer: One triple bond (or two double bonds)
questions.explanation: Consuming 2 moles of H₂ per mole of hydrocarbon indicates a degree of unsaturation of 2, corresponding to one C≡C triple bond (e.g. 1-butyne or 2-butyne) or two double bonds (butadiene).

questions.question: How many structural isomers (including chain and positional isomers) exist for the alkene with molecular formula C₄H₈?
questions.explanation: C₄H₈ acyclic alkene structural isomers are: (1) CH₂=CH—CH₂—CH₃ (1-butene), (2) CH₃—CH=CH—CH₃ (2-butene), and (3) CH₂=C(CH₃)₂ (2-methylpropene / isobutylene).

questions.question: During complete stoichiometric combustion of 1 mole of propane gas (C₃H₈), how many moles of oxygen (O₂) gas are consumed and how many moles of H₂O are produced?
questions.explanation: Balanced equation: C₃H₈(g) + 5O₂(g) → 3CO₂(g) + 4H₂O(g). Exactly 5 moles of O₂ are consumed to form 3 moles CO₂ and 4 moles H₂O.

questions.question: What gas is evolved with effervescence when a small pellet of sodium metal is dropped into absolute ethanol?
questions.explanation: Sodium displaces hydrogen from the hydroxyl group of ethanol to produce hydrogen gas: 2Na + 2C₂H₅OH -> 2C2H5ONa + H₂.

questions.question: What organic product is obtained when ethanol is heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K (170 °C)?
questions.explanation: At 443 K, conc. H₂SO₄ dehydrates ethanol to ethene: CH3CH₂OH -> CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O.

questions.question: Why is concentrated sulphuric acid referred to as a 'dehydrating agent' in the conversion of ethanol to ethene?
options: It chemically extracts a water molecule (H₂O) from the ethanol molecule.
It cools the reaction down to absolute zero.
It acts as a source of oxygen.
questions.answer: It chemically extracts a water molecule (H₂O) from the ethanol molecule.
questions.explanation: A dehydrating agent removes the elements of water (H and OH) from a compound.

questions.question: Why is the ingestion of even small quantities of methanol (CH₃OH) lethal to humans?
options: Methanol turns into solid diamond in the stomach.
Methanol is oxidised by liver enzymes to methanal (formaldehyde), which coagulates cellular protoplasm and destroys the optic nerve.
Methanol removes all calcium from bones.
questions.answer: Methanol is oxidised by liver enzymes to methanal (formaldehyde), which coagulates cellular protoplasm and destroys the optic nerve.
questions.explanation: Methanal coagulates biological proteins and destroys the optic nerve, causing blindness and death.

questions.question: What is 'denatured alcohol'?
options: Commercial ethanol rendered poisonous and undrinkable by adding methanol, pyridine, and copper sulphate dye
A mixture of ethanol and sugar
questions.answer: Commercial ethanol rendered poisonous and undrinkable by adding methanol, pyridine, and copper sulphate dye
questions.explanation: Denaturing prevents industrial tax-free alcohol from being diverted for illegal drinking by making it toxic and foul-tasting.

title: Ethanoic Acid, Esterification, Saponification, Soaps & Detergents
tagline: Fruity esters, soap micelle cleansing action, and hard water scum prevention.
theoryHtml:
1. Ethanoic Acid (Acetic Acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$):

  • Vinegar: A $5\text{ to }8\%$ solution of ethanoic acid in water is called vinegar, widely used as a culinary condiment and food preservative.
  • Glacial Acetic Acid: Pure ethanoic acid has a melting point of $290\text{ K}$ ($17\ ^\circ\text{C}$). During cold winter weather, it freezes into ice-like crystalline sheets, earning the name glacial acetic acid.

2. Esterification Reaction:

Ethanoic acid reacts with absolute ethanol in the presence of an acid catalyst (conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) to form an ester called ethyl ethanoate:

$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{Conc. }\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{COOC}_2\text{H}_5 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Esters are sweet-smelling, pleasant, and fruity substances used in perfumes, fragrances, and flavoring essences.

3. Saponification (Soap Preparation):

When an ester is heated with a strong alkali (sodium hydroxide), it hydrolyses back into alcohol and the sodium salt of carboxylic acid:

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COOC}_2\text{H}_5 + \text{NaOH} \longrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COONa} + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$$

Because this reaction is used in the preparation of soaps from natural fats (esters of glycerol), it is called saponification.

4. Reaction with Sodium Bicarbonate (Test for Acids):

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{NaHCO}_3 \longrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COONa} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2 \uparrow$$

Brisk effervescence of carbon dioxide gas that turns lime water milky confirms the presence of a carboxylic acid.

5. Cleansing Action of Soaps & Micelles:

  • Soap Molecule Structure: A soap molecule (e.g. sodium stearate, $\text{C}_{17}\text{H}_{35}\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$) has two distinct ends:
    1. A long hydrocarbon tail: hydrophobic (water-repelling) and lipophilic (oil-loving).
    2. An ionic carboxylate head ($-\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$): hydrophilic (water-loving).
  • Micelle Formation: In water, soap molecules assemble into spherical clusters called micelles. The hydrophobic hydrocarbon tails cluster inward, embedding themselves in the oily dirt droplet, while the ionic hydrophilic heads project outward in water. The oily dirt is trapped inside the micelle core as a stable emulsion and rinsed away by water.
  • Hard Water & Scum: Hard water contains dissolved calcium ($\text{Ca}^{2+}$) and magnesium ($\text{Mg}^{2+}$) ions. These ions react with soap to form an insoluble, curdy white precipitate called scum, wasting soap and hindering lather.
  • Synthetic Detergents: Detergents are sodium salts of alkyl sulphonic acids or ammonium salts with chloride/bromide ions. Their charged ends do not form insoluble precipitates with $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ and $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, allowing them to remain completely effective even in hard water (used in shampoos and laundry detergents).
pointsToRemember: Vinegar is 5-8% ethanoic acid in water; pure ethanoic acid freezes at 17 °C (glacial acetic acid).
Esterification: Ethanoic acid + Ethanol → Ethyl ethanoate (fruity ester) + H₂O.
Soap molecules form micelles (hydrophobic tails trap oil, hydrophilic heads face water); synthetic detergents work in hard water without forming scum.
keyNotes: Board Distinction: Test for carboxylic acid vs alcohol: Add NaHCO₃; carboxylic acid produces brisk effervescence of CO₂ turning lime water milky; alcohol shows no reaction.

questions.question: A neutral organic compound 'P' with formula C₃H₆O does not react with sodium metal and does not react with NaHCO₃. On reduction, it forms a secondary alcohol (propan-2-ol). Identify 'P':
questions.explanation: Ketones (CH₃COCH₃, propanone) reduce to secondary alcohols (propan-2-ol). Aldehydes reduce to primary alcohols.

questions.question: What is the correct order of increasing boiling points among the following four-carbon compounds: Butane, Butanal, Butan-1-ol, and Butanoic acid?
questions.explanation: Non-polar alkane (weak van der Waals) < Dipolar aldehyde (dipole-dipole) < Alcohol (intermolecular H-bonding) < Carboxylic acid (dimeric double H-bonding).

questions.question: When 4.6 g of pure sodium metal (atomic mass = 23 u) is reacted completely with excess absolute ethanol, what volume of dry H₂ gas is evolved at STP (1 mole gas at STP = 22.4 L)?
questions.explanation: 4.6 g Na = 4.6 / 23 = 0.2 moles Na. 2Na + 2C₂H₅OH → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂. 2 moles Na yield 1 mole H₂. Thus, 0.2 moles Na yield 0.1 mole H₂ = 0.1 × 22.4 L = 2.24 L.

questions.question: Why does the reaction of ethanoic acid with ethanol to form ethyl ethanoate require a few drops of concentrated sulphuric acid?
options: H₂SO₄ acts both as an acid catalyst and as a dehydrating agent to absorb water and drive equilibrium forward
H₂SO₄ oxidises ethanol to ethanoic acid
H₂SO₄ turns the ester into soap
H₂SO₄ changes the boiling point of ethanol
questions.answer: H₂SO₄ acts both as an acid catalyst and as a dehydrating agent to absorb water and drive equilibrium forward
questions.explanation: Esterification is a reversible equilibrium. Concentrated H₂SO₄ provides H⁺ ions to catalyse the reaction and absorbs H₂O byproduct, shifting equilibrium towards ester synthesis (Le Chatelier's principle).

questions.question: Synthetic diamonds are manufactured industrially by subjecting pure carbon to which extreme conditions?
options: Zero gravity and cryogenic liquid helium
Very high temperature and very high pressure
questions.answer: Very high temperature and very high pressure
questions.explanation: Synthetic diamonds are fabricated by subjecting pure carbon to ultra-high pressures (~50,000–100,000 atm) and temperatures (~1500–2500°C), converting graphite into diamond crystals indistinguishable from natural gems.

questions.question: What is the commercial name given to pure anhydrous ethanoic acid because it freezes into ice-like sheets at 17 °C (290 K)?
questions.explanation: Pure ethanoic acid has a melting point of 17 °C (290 K) and forms crystalline ice-like sheets in cold climates, hence 'glacial'.

questions.question: What characteristic physical sensory property distinguishes esters from their parent carboxylic acids and alcohols?
options: A pungent smell of rotten eggs
A sweet, pleasant, and fruity aroma
questions.answer: A sweet, pleasant, and fruity aroma
questions.explanation: Esters possess sweet, fruity aromas and are widely employed in perfumes, confectioneries, and flavourings.

questions.question: How can a student chemically distinguish between a sample of ethanol and a sample of ethanoic acid in two unlabelled test tubes?
options: By testing electrical conductivity in dry air
By adding sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO₃); ethanoic acid produces brisk effervescence of CO₂ gas, while ethanol shows no reaction
questions.answer: By adding sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO₃); ethanoic acid produces brisk effervescence of CO₂ gas, while ethanol shows no reaction
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid reacts with NaHCO₃ with brisk effervescence of CO₂ (turning lime water milky); ethanol does not react.

questions.question: What happens when a soap solution is used for washing clothes in hard water containing calcium and magnesium salts?
options: Soap produces double the amount of lather.
Calcium and magnesium ions react with soap to precipitate an insoluble, sticky white curdy substance called 'scum'.
questions.answer: Calcium and magnesium ions react with soap to precipitate an insoluble, sticky white curdy substance called 'scum'.
questions.explanation: Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ precipitate soap molecules as insoluble calcium/magnesium stearate (scum), hindering cleaning.

questions.question: Why are synthetic detergents able to clean effectively even in hard water, unlike traditional soaps?
options: The charged sulphonate or ammonium ends of detergents do not form insoluble precipitates with calcium and magnesium ions present in hard water.
Detergents evaporate immediately upon contact with water.
questions.answer: The charged sulphonate or ammonium ends of detergents do not form insoluble precipitates with calcium and magnesium ions present in hard water.
questions.explanation: Calcium and magnesium salts of sulphonic acids are water-soluble, so detergents lather freely and clean without forming scum.
